sections.title: Management of Orbital Blow Out Fractures

branches: 1. Observation, oral antibiotics, ice packs, nasal decongestants, patient is instructed not to blow out nose
2. Systemic steroids for sever orbital edema compromising optic n
3. Prevention of permanent vertical diplopia and cosemetically unacceptable enophthalmos

sections.title: Clinical Decision Matrix: Blowout Fractures
content: Small cracks without herniation —> observation
Fractures involving one half of orbital floor with little or no herniation no enophthalmos, no diplopia do not require treatment
Fractures > 1/2 of the orbital floor may develop enophthalmos if left untreated
Fractures with entrapment of orbital contents enophthalmos >2mm and persistent diplopia in primary position should be repaired within 2 weeks
Patient with diplopia and tissue incarceration but without muscle entrapment improvement often occur without surgery
White eyed fracture is a subgroup for which urgent repair is required to avoid permanent vertical diplopia neuromuscular damage

sections.title: Supplemental: Differential Diagnosis of Orbital Trauma

rows: Rock hard lids, afferent pupillary defect (APD)
Decreased vision, APD, normal appearing orbit

sections.title: EMERGENCY: Lateral Canthotomy & Cantholysis
content: Indication: Treatment of retrobulbar hge (hemorrhage)
Step 1: Clamping the incision site for 60 seconds
Step 2: 1-2 cm horizontal full thickness incision under local anaesthesia (1-2ml lidocaine 1-2% with adrenaline) at the angle of lateral canthus

Step 3: The lower lid is retracted downwards and the inferior crust of lateral canthal tendon is cut using blunt tipped scissors directed inferiorly and inserted adjacent and parallel to lateral orbital rim between conjunctiva and skin angled away from eyeball
Step 4: Blood gently encouraged to drain
Step 5: If necessary the superior limb of tendon can also cut but carry risk of damage to adnex structures.

sections.title: Thyroid Eye Disease (TED): Activity & Severity
sections.content: Treatment of thyroid eye disease depends on clinical activity, severity, and duration of orbitopathy. Essential first steps include: Patient counselling on aim, expectations, benefits and risk of different therapy, and absolute cessation of smoking in all cases.

rows: Lubricants, Topical anti-inflammatory agents, Selenium daily for 6 months, Head elevation (3 pillows) to reduce periorbital edema, Eyelid tapping during sleep

Consider treatment for 3/7 activity or more. Systemic steroids 60-80mg/day initially then tapering; long term low dose may be needed. Low dose fractionated radiotherapy (2nd line). Combined therapy: steroids+azathioprine+low dose prednisolone

sections.title: TED: Optic Neuropathy & Post-Inflammatory Complications
content: C. Optic Neuropathy: Pulsed methyl prednisolone IV 0.5-1g on three successive days
C. Optic Neuropathy: Conversion to oral 40mg/day + liver function monitoring + gastric & osteoporosis prophylaxis
C. Optic Neuropathy: Second line (steroid resistance/persistent disease): monoclonal antibody (teprotumumab)
D. Post-Inflammatory Complications: Orbital decompression

D. Strabismus Surgery: For persistent diplopia in primary or reading position after 6-12m from inflammation; until then use prisms or botulinum toxin (recession of inferior and medial rectus) with adjustable sutures
D. Lid Surgery (Mild): Improve by control of hyperthyroidism
D. Lid Surgery (Moderate): Botulinum toxin injection levator aponeurosis and muller muscle, prisms
D. Lid Surgery (Severe): Recession/disinsertion of muller muscle in severe lid retraction

sections.title: Senile Entropion Treatment
content: Temporary: Lubricant, taping, bandage soft contact lens
Chemodenervation: Orbicularis botulinum toxin
Surgical (Overriding/Disinsertion): Transverse everting sutures
Surgical (Durable): Wies procedure (full thickness horizontal lid splitting + insertion of everting sutures)
Lower lid retraction reinsertion: Reserved for recurrence
Horizontal lid laxity: Lateral tarsal sling, full thickness lateral pentagon excision, Tightening

branches: Main Features: Enophthalmos, Upper lid ptosis, Superior sulcus hollowing, Sagging of lower lid
Surgical: Silicon block in inferior orbit (if implant present)
Non-Surgical: Intermittent injection of filler (hyaluronic acid) into orbital apex
Lower Lid: Correction of laxity by lateral tarsal sling (strip)

sections.title: Surgical Process: Levator Advancement
content: 1. Mark level of desired post-op lid crease and peak position
2. Subcutaneous local anesthesia
3. Skin incision at predetermined skin crease level
4. Divide orbicularis/septum; retract fat pads to expose LPS
5. Free LPS from tarsus and underlying Muller muscle
6. Dissect to expose superior tarsus
7. Advance aponeurosis and suture to tarsus (6/0 vicryl); check lid eversion
8. Observe and adjust position in awake patient
9. Lid crease formation (orbicularis-levator-orbicularis suture)
10. Close skin incision (6/0 or 7/0 vicryl), remove at 1 week
